title: Smoothing normal on GPU (using geometry shader) without knowledge to adjacent faces
body_excerpt: Smoothing normal on GPU might be a common question because you really can generate flat normal by triangle primitives , but you don't have adjacent faces so it is not possible to smooth normal . I went into this topic without deep thinking . Now I encountered a problem . Basically , what I thought was : You don't have to know adjacent faces . The only thing you need to do is adding known normal which was generated by the only known triangle to the vertex that you want to generate smooth normal for . It's nice that when you're processing primitives , you can also access its vertices . If you go through all faces , for the vertices that were shared between primitives , you will access the same ID , and then you will add each faces' flattened normal to them . Finally , you got all vertices summing up with all their related faces' normal , then just normalize them . It sounds quite nice because you don't have to require adjacent faces . You just add known information, and generate smoothed normal using mathematical tool (normalize). [CODE] ... [CODE] But there's a problem . What I was going to do is performing addition without knowing operand . Addition requires two operands , one is the flattened normal , but the other is the 'original' or 'already-existed' normal .
